question.text: Mark-to-Market for illiquid securities in a Cat III AIF is typically NOT at full Fair Market Value; the manager must instead apply:

answer.text: The last traded price regardless of volume
A valuation method approved by the registered valuer reflecting illiquidity, e.g., PV of expected realisable proceeds over multiple trading days

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the chapter: 'valuation of illiquid securities shall not be done on the basis of the Fair Market Value of the security. The Investment Manager shall clearly state the Valuation Method adopted by the fund for the valuation of illiquid securities, approved by a registered valuer.' One example method is PV of disposal proceeds over days. **The Trap:** Last traded price is exactly what the rule precludes; book value of issuer is unrelated; arbitrary 50% haircut is not approved. **Cross-Exam Context:** Side-pocket accounting is Cat III-specific. XIX-D (Cat I/II) handles quarterly valuation differently. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When a material holding becomes illiquid mid-quarter (trading suspended, credit event, listing downgrade), segregate it into a side-pocket immediately - new subscriptions/redemptions then occur only on the 'main' NAV, protecting all parties.
